newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Kuwait to shed holdings in Real Estate Bank. [CORRECTED 8:28 16/10]
newsitem.headline: Kuwait to shed holdings in Real Estate Bank. [CORRECTED 8:28 16/10]

text.p: (Replaces erroneous story which referred to Industrial Bank of Kuwait).
Kuwait will sell most of its stake in Kuwait Real Estate Bank (KREB) in a two-stage privatisation bid, the Kuwait News Agency (KUNA) reported on Tuesday.

The Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA), the state investment arm, will sell 30 million of its 100 million KREB shares by public auction in November and another 60 million by subscription at a later stage, the agency reported.
Kuwait has 32.9 percent stake in KREB, which mainly extends medium- and long-term loans to construction and commercial projects and property investment. It is also a retail bank.
KIA has set the starting price for the November auction at 410 fils ($1.37), KUNA said. There are 1,000 fils to the dinar.
KREB shares closed on Tuesday at 390 fils.
The bank had reported a 101.8 percent rise in net profit in the first half of 1996 compared to the same period last year, rising to 3.5 million dinars.

The sale is part of Kuwait's plan to shed state holdings in about 60 local firms and public services such as electricity, water and telecommunications. The plan, announced after the 1991 Gulf War, is supervised by KIA.
